In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin, in the presence of ethanol, inhibits gluconeogenesis, ketogenesis and amino acid catabolism in perfused rat liver.
insulin inhibits ethanol-induced hyperglycemia in perfused rat livers by lowering hepatic ketogenesis, gluconeogenesis and by increasing the oxidation of fatty acids.
the effect of insulin on ethanol-induced hyperglycemia is due to a direct action on the liver and is not mediated by the peripheral circulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
insulin, in the presence of ethanol, opposes the hyperglycaemic, hyperketonaemic and lipolytic effects of ethanol.
insulin opposes ethanol-induced hyperglycemia and ketogenesis and raises serum amino acids and fatty acids.
insulin, infused alone, opposes ethanol-induced hyperglycemia by lowering hepatic gluconeogenesis, ketogenesis and amino acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ethanol-induced hyperglycemia is due to the increased gluconeogenic capacity of the liver.
insulin is a powerful inhibitor of the hyperglycaemic effects of ethanol.
the effects of insulin on the hepatic metabolism of amino acids are more complex than previously thought and are dependent on the nutritional state of the animal.
